title: Meng Tian, Qin general of the northern frontier
summary: General of the state of Qin under the First Emperor, sent north with a reported 300,000 troops against the Xiongnu. He secured the area north of the Ordos bend of the Yellow River, set up garrisons and oversaw linking of the Great Wall. After the emperor died he was forced to take his own life in 210 BCE.

uncertainty.note: No birth date is given by the sources opened. The span runs from the 214 BC order to link the walls (Encyclopedia.com) to his death in 210 BCE (ChinaKnowledge, 210 BCE = astronomical -209). It is his documented career, not his lifespan.

as_recorded.value: In 214 b.c., ... Qin Shihuangdi, ordered his general Meng Tian

where.modern_name: Ordos region, Inner Mongolia, China (centre of modern Ordos City)
where.historical_name: Region north of the great Ordos bend of the Yellow River, northern frontier of the Qin empire

importance.justification: Commander of Qin's northern frontier and the general associated with linking the early Great Wall.
